column2: req_desc

Home tour
Starting from the starting content, a visitor reads `/` top to bottom, jumps to every section from the header and from the intro, and lands on each section heading with focus, clear of the header.

Starting home content
`/` shows its sections, headings, intro, About, background list, principles and footer exactly as published in Seed data, in published order.

Section jumps clear of the header
Every section jump by link or by an address with a hash puts focus on the section heading at least 16 px below the header, within one second, and instantly with reduced motion and on load.

Current section while scrolling
The header and menu link of the section holding the point 40% down the viewport carries `aria-current="true"`, updating while scrolling down and back up, and no link is current while the intro holds that point.

Editorial paper look
Every page reads as a quiet editorial page: warm off-white paper, hairline rules and no shadows, oversized ragged serif headlines, equal-width figures in statistics and indexes, on a twelve-column grid with project titles hanging into the left margin.

Reading the statistics
A product manager scrolls to About, watches the four statistics count up to their published values and steps through them by keyboard to read each note and its parts.

Statistics count
Each statistic counts from 0 to its value over 1,200 ms on the published curve once per page load, its tab's name always carries the final value, and with reduced motion the values show at once.

Statistics tabs by keyboard
The `Statistics` tab list selects tabs at once with ArrowRight, ArrowLeft, Home and End, wrapping, with one Tab stop and the panel left out of the Tab order.

Statistic part bars
The selected statistic's panel shows its note, one bar segment per part sized to the part's share within 0.5 percentage points, and each part as `<part label>: <part value>` text.

Scoping a Brand Identity engagement
A brand lead opens Brand Identity by keyboard, reads its capabilities, deliverables and typical engagement, and follows `Start a Brand Identity project` from the open panel into a form with that project type checked while the service stays open.

Services collapsed at load
Every service is collapsed at load unless the address names one, and nothing inside a collapsed panel can be reached by Tab or by a screen reader.

Published service content
Each open service panel shows its summary, capabilities, deliverables, typical engagement and two links exactly as published, with the two lists side by side from 768 px wide and stacked below.

Service panel motion
A service panel opens and closes by changing height over 280 to 360 ms while its chevron turns half a turn, and does both at once with reduced motion.

Comparing Website Design
A brand lead moves between service buttons by arrow keys, opens Website Design so the open service closes, and shares an address that reopens it with focus on its button.

Service buttons by arrow keys
ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End move focus between the service buttons, wrapping, without opening or closing any service.

One open service in the address
At most one service is open, its id is kept in the `service` parameter without a new history entry while other parameters and the hash stay, and an address with `service=<id>` opens it with focus on its button.

Digital Product evidence
A product manager follows `See Digital Product Design work` to the gallery filtered and announced for that service, and after the principal designer's content change sees counts and lists that agree.

Service work link
Following `See <service name> work` on `/` checks that category, jumps to `Selected work` with focus on its heading and makes the filter announcement.

Category counts follow content
After any content change through the grading route, the next page load shows each filter radio's count equal to the projects listed under it, and an empty category shows the published empty sentence.

Grading content route
The grading route replaces, restores and lists content and enquiries with the published key, shapes, statuses and error order, as qualified in API.

Filtering the work
A brand lead filters the work by each service with the arrow keys, hears each count announced, reloads the filtered address and finds the same category checked.

Filter radios and announcements
The `Filter work by service` radios move with arrow keys and clicks, show only the chosen projects in published order and make the published plural, singular or empty announcement once per change.

Filter in the address
The chosen category is kept in the `category` parameter without a new history entry, an address with a category opens with it checked and announces nothing, and an unknown category is ignored.

Hidden projects unreachable
Projects outside the chosen category cannot be reached by Tab or by a screen reader, and the gallery shows three, two or one column by width as published.

Opening a case study
A brand lead opens a work item by keyboard, sees its cover carried into the case study's hero, the title lines rise, the address change and focus land on the heading, then reads every section.

Cover Carry motion
Opening a case study from a work item keeps the document loaded, adds one history entry, sets the title and focus, and moves the hero from the cover's box to its own over 440 to 520 ms before the title lines rise.

Case study content
Each `/work/<slug>` shows its eyebrow, title, standfirst, hero and the six sections with the project's stored content in published order.

On this page navigation
The `On this page` links jump to their sections with focus on the heading clear of the header, and the link of the section holding the point 40% down the viewport is current.

Not-found pages
An unknown project and any other unknown page answer HTTP 404 with their published heading, link and title.

Moving through the work
A brand lead inside a filtered sequence steps from project to project with the links and arrow keys, then presses Back once per case study shown to return to the gallery tile of the project they first opened.

Previous and next project links
`More work` names the previous and next projects of the current sequence, omits them at the ends, keeps the `category` parameter and follows content changes on the next page load.

Arrow keys between projects
ArrowLeft and ArrowRight on a case study open the previous and next project unless focus is in a text field, select, radio group or tab list.

Back to the same tile
After one browser Back press per case study shown, arriving on `/` keeps the chosen filter, scrolls the item of the project first opened from the gallery fully into view clear of the header, moves the cover back into it and focuses its link.

Neighbour slide motion
Moving to the previous or next project slides the old hero 40 px out and the new one 40 px in on the published sides over 320 to 400 ms, then raises the title lines.

Motion tour
A visitor loads `/`, watches the intro lines rise and the headings and covers reveal while scrolling, hovers and focuses work items, and scrolls the intro plate down and back.

Intro and reveal motion
The intro lines, section headings and covers reveal once per page load with the published offsets, durations and staggers.

Work item hover and focus
Hovering or focusing a work item scales its cover to 1.04 and raises its `View case study` caption within the published times, and leaving or blurring reverses both.

Intro plate follows scroll
The intro plate is moved down by round(0.25 × min(s, 800)) px at scroll position s and returns exactly when scrolling back.

Reduced motion end states
With reduced motion every published motion happens at once without movement or fade, the plate stays at 0, and end states, focus, announcements and addresses match the motion version.

Keyboard-only enquiry
A brand lead goes through the site with only the keyboard, from the skip link through the menu, a service, the filter and a case study, to one sent enquiry after pressing Enter twice on `Send enquiry`.

Tab order and skip link
The first Tab stops on `/` follow the published order at each width, and `Skip to content` is the first stop, visible while focused, and moves focus to the level-1 heading.

Focus visible and clear of the header
Every focused control shows a visible ring at least 2 px wide with 3:1 contrast, and each one outside the header and the open menu is scrolled so its top edge is at least 72 px from the viewport top.

Menu dialog by keyboard
Below 1024 px the `Menu` dialog opens with focus on `About`, keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside, closes on Escape or `Close menu` with focus back on `Menu`, and is unreachable while closed.

Phone visit
A product manager on a 375 px phone opens the menu by tap, opens a service and a filter by tap, and swipes through a case study's showcase screens by finger.

Phone layout and tap targets
At 375x812 there is no horizontal page overflow, every control is at least 44 by 44 px, and the work, statistics, process and service lists follow the phone layout.

Showcase by finger and buttons
A sideways swipe of 60 px or more, or a showcase button, moves exactly one screen, updates the counter and `data-screen` and announces the screen.

Menu by tap
A tap on `Menu` opens the menu sliding down, and a tap on `Close menu`, on a menu link or outside the panel closes it the same way as Escape.

Procedural plates
Every cover, hero, showcase screen, portrait and intro plate is a deliberate composition drawn from the project's hue and motif, distinct per project and the same on the tile and in the hero.

Sending a commission brief
A brand lead fills the enquiry form, corrects the published validation messages, sends it and sees the thank-you panel with the reference and stored values, while the mail server receives both messages.

Enquiry checks
Sending the form with failed checks sends nothing and shows the error box, links, messages and `aria-invalid` exactly as published, and the server rejects the same values with 422.

One enquiry per submission
Pressing `Send enquiry` any number of times while pending, or sending again after a failure, creates one enquiry, one reference and one pair of messages.

Studio copy and acknowledgement
Each sent enquiry reaches the mail server as a studio copy and then an acknowledgement with the published recipients, subjects and text carrying the stored values character for character.

Saved without mail and not saved
With the mail server unreachable the enquiry is kept with mail `not_sent` and the panel shows the delay alert, and when the request itself fails the form keeps its values and shows the not-saved alert.

Three-viewport review
A reviewer looks at `/`, a case study and `/privacy` at 1280x800, 768x1024 and 375x812, finds the published layout at each, and downloads a brief PDF from a sent enquiry.

Brief PDF
The brief address answers a one-page PDF rendered from the stored enquiry with the published file name and text, and an unknown token answers 404.

Brief outage and health
With Gotenberg unreachable the brief address answers the published 503 page while enquiries still send, and `/api/health` reports `ok` or `unavailable` with status 200.

Page structure and accessibility
Every page has `lang="en"`, one `main`, one level-1 heading, its published title and no automated accessibility violations, and the server keeps the published boundary.

Source integrity
The source reads every credential and service address from the environment, sends each enquiry and renders each brief through the real services, and draws every plate from project data.
`/app/run.json` exists, with string fields `install`, `build` and `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`, and its commands install, build and serve the app.

`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at `/app` lists every shipped package with its licence, plus the two font families; shipped packages means the production dependency tree reported by `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`.

Every shipped package uses the MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or 0BSD licence, except `@fontsource/instrument-serif` and `@fontsource/instrument-sans`, which are under the SIL Open Font Licence and supply the font files the app serves.
The app stores data only in the provided Postgres database and uses no other datastore, such as SQLite, Redis, or local files for content or enquiries.
The app uses no animation library, no WebGL, no canvas animation loop and no video.
Every colour in the stylesheets is written in hex or rgb/rgba notation, with no colour-mixing or other colour functions.
The provided service setup and its dev credentials are left unchanged, and no credentials are committed in source files.
